summary: Independent English review of FR-2.8 (spec.md line 120) for Level 2 Unit 2, weeks 9 to 16 (Phase 1, P1, track storytime_l2_unit2_20261106). Input: the English review extract (Task 1.11 PDF, 207 pages, SHA-256 f25e0846dc1223064bee8027450aeaaff87f5aa7ff35a67b0af6b5a62359fa2e, verified) and QUESTIONS.txt; audited HEAD 819f1613704982354def9ee5aea1bc0a2e9d6ba5 equals HEAD. I read the full extract (9,974 lines, 8 weeks, days 1 to 5, songs, benchmark, review pages, reading records) and checked each week against Tasks 1.2 to 1.9, the unit 1 files (English fields only), and design section 2. Verdict: the scope, the decodability, the English quality, the scripts, the songs, the review strips, the check items, and the week 16 benchmark all pass. Both hand rules of FR-2.8 hold for all 8 weeks (each review strip card is taught by its week, judged against the real teaching sequence, not the card week fields; each check item has exactly one right picture). The writer's defaults Q-A to Q-E, U3, and U4 are sound; Daniel decides them with the text. No Blocker and no Major. I report 5 Nits: a duplicated materials entry (week 9), a picture-count question on page 2 of The Den (week 11), tautological where-questions in D3 (weeks 12 to 15), 'Color the jump.' (week 13), and the week 17 Script E dependency that the unit 3 track must honor (week 16).

L2U2-W11-1 [Nit] PDF page 68 (C4) and page 205 (reading record), week 11 decodable 'The Den', page 2: 'Ten men in the den!'. The story family is Tom, Mom, and Dad (pages 1, 3 to 5), so the text names ten men that the story never shows again. If the page 2 picture prompt shows ten men (FR-2.3: the object counts that the text says), the text and the picture match and the line is a playful count; if the prompt shows only the family, the count word misleads the children. The unit read hand-checked only the last two pages of each book (unit-read.md, method step 3), so nobody has compared this page with its prompt yet. Forge has not rendered the unit 2 rows (the owner gate is open), so a prompt fix is still cheap. Fix: the writer checks the page 2 prompt of 'The Den' and either makes the picture show ten men (for example ten toy men in the den) or changes the line (for example 'Dad is in the den!').

L2U2-W12-1 [Nit] PDF page 99 (week 12 D3; the same pattern on page 125 week 13, page 177 week 15, and page 151 week 14): the where-question of the D3 routine has a tautological answer: 'Where is Nan? Point to the picture. — answer: Nan (page 9)' (week 12); 'Where is the child who can jump? — answer: jump (page 4)' (week 13); 'Where is it rainy? — answer: rainy (page 6)' (week 14); 'Where is the boat? — answer: boat (page 8)' (week 15). The pointing task works in class, and the loops-questions routine needs a where-question, but the printed answer names the thing, not the place. Week 11 shows the good form: 'Where is Pat? — answer: sofa (page 7)'. Fix: name the place in the answer (for example 'Where is Nan? — at the table (page 9)') or reword the question to Who or What ('Who has the book? — Nan (page 9)').

L2U2-W13-1 [Nit] PDF page 126, week 13 D4, part 1: 'Color the jump.' The other six weeks name a thing ('Color the cake.', 'Color the hat.', 'Color the cat.', 'Color the book.', 'Color the sun.', 'Color the bus.'). 'The jump' uses the action word as a thing name, and 'draw you: run, kick, or clap' in the same step is also informal. Both are clear in class; the polish is small. Fix: 'Color the picture of the jump.' or 'Color Sam.' and 'Now draw yourself: run, kick, or clap.'.

L2U2-W16-1 [Nit] PDF page 185 (day 1, before this lesson) and page 201 (benchmark, absent child): the week 16 text sends the Benchmark 2 sittings of the children after number 27 and of absent children to 'the week 17 Script E slot'. Week 17 is unit 3, which no track has written yet. Unit 1 set the same dependency ('the others go to the week 9 Script E slot') and week 9 honored it (E2 of week 9 runs the waiting Benchmark 1 sittings with the week 8 forms), so the pattern works when the next week knows about it. Fix: no text change; the orchestrator relays the dependency to the unit 3 track so that the week 17 Script E holds the waiting Benchmark 2 sittings with the week 16 forms.

Week 16 (Task 1.9, PDF pages 183 to 207): the review week in the shape of w08. Block weeks 9 to 15; days 1 to 4 cover them all (9+10, 11+12, 13+14, 15 plus the weakest week from the Friday checks, as w08 day 4 does); day 5 is the child's choice. Medleys come from the block songs and every unit 2 song appears at least once; day 4 pairs the week 15 song with a repeat, exactly as w08 day 4 does. Benchmark 2 keeps the week 8 shape: paper part 10 minutes with 8 circle-picture rows and 12 write-letter boxes (the 12 taught letters n, a, p, m, s, t, o, d, e, h, f, g), pass 6 of 8 pictures and 8 of 12 letters (the week 8 share 5 of 7, rounded down); one-to-one 3 minutes (2 plus the 1-minute reading record) with the 26-letter strip (pass 20 of 26, the same as week 8), the 12 sound cards (pass 10 of 12, the week 8 share 6 of 7 rounded down), and 4 blend words dog, hen, fed, hat (pass 3 of 4, as week 8); reading record of the 7 block decodables, copied word for word (I compared all 7 texts in the PDF with the C4 pages), pass 90 percent; class record sheet of 30 rows; 27 sittings (3 on day 1, then 6 a day), the rest to the week 17 Script E slot. All 8 benchmark picture rows have exactly one right picture (doll/sun/cup; cat/egg/bus; pen/fish/horse; dog/sun/foot; bag/cup/sun; cat/bed/fish; sun/cup/pot; fan/dog/cup). The 5 review pages: every circle-word answer is one of its printed choices, and every picture sort is correct (day 2 asks for the middle sound /a/ vs /e/; day 5 shows one picture for each of the 7 unit 2 elements). Home card 'Unit 2 is done...' as the spec asks.

Hand rule 1 (each review strip card is taught by its week; FR-2.8, tech debt finding 3): I read the review strip of every day of weeks 9 to 16 in the extract and compared each card label with the real teaching sequence (letters n, a, p, m, s, t, o in unit 1; d in week 9; e in week 11; h in week 12; f in week 14; g in week 15; the 19 unit 1 tricky words; the unit 2 tricky words of weeks 9 to 15; the word cards man (week 10) and pot (week 13); the frames of weeks 7 to 15), not with the week fields that the checker trusts. Every card of every day is taught by its week. The daily recall sets (5 cards a day) are also all taught to date. The rule holds for all 8 weeks.

Hand rule 2 (each check item has exactly one right picture; FR-2.8, tech debt finding 9): I checked every picture row by hand: the E5 rows of weeks 9 to 15 (3 rows each), the 8 benchmark rows of week 16, and the picture sorts of the 5 review pages. Each row has exactly one picture with the target sound in the target position; each sort group holds only pictures of its sound. The rule holds for all 8 weeks.

Defaults judged (QUESTIONS.txt and plan lines 168 to 176): Q-A (the frame word 'Yum' counts with the frame): accept. The design itself puts 'Yum!' in the week 9 frame, the gate (design 6.2, 90 percent) is not machine-checked (tech debt of 2026-10-22), and the gate already excepts family words and names; without the exception the read-along sits at 65 percent. Daniel decides with the text. Q-B ('goes' moves from week 12 to week 14 because a sight-word step holds at most 3 words): accept. Week 12 keeps 3 new words (it, said, that), week 14 has room (you), and no week 12 text needs 'goes'; the schema change is the heavier route. Q-C (frame 'I can ___.' for 'I can run/hop/jump.'): accept; frameCount cannot match slash words, and run, jump, and hop stay in the book and the song. Q-D (frame 'It is ___.' for 'It is hot/cold.'): accept; same slash limit, and the weeks differ in family (colors vs weather) and story. Q-E (12 letter boxes, pass 8 of 12; sound cards 10 of 12): accept; the benchmark check needs the 12 taught letters, and the pass marks keep the week 8 shares rounded down. U3 (the two 'on a person' twists): accept; unit 1 has the pattern 4 times and the things and persons differ. U4 (week 11 and week 7 both find Pip): accept; hide-and-seek behind Nan vs a guess under a blanket are different stories and twists.

Plan claims verified (A5): unit-read-stage-checks.txt (the Task 1.10 gate capture) matches the plan lines: st2/9 to st2/15 38 PASS each, st2/16 18 PASS, 'Summary: 16 package(s), 0 failed check(s), 2 warning(s)', the two warnings being the allowed print-missing of st2/8 and st2/16 (FR-3.3). The self-check reports (w09 to w16) match what I found in the extract: book texts, page word counts, check items, strips, song titles, and family words. One self-check difference is explained by the print design, not a data error: the w16 self-check quotes the raw picture-sort groups (3 pictures a group) while the PDF answer key names the 2 targets that the student page prints (review-rows.ts: 'the teacher key names only the pictures that the student page prints in the row', the unit 1 rule A-48 part F F3). The guard denied my own STAGE_CHECKS rerun, so the capture is the gate evidence; my hand checks above cover the two hand rules that the checker cannot see.

English quality for Anuban 3 (about 5 years old): the teacher language is short, natural, and correct; every step is doable in its minutes (the main steps fill 24 minutes in all 40 teaching-day scripts that I checked); the stories are clear with real twists; no week title, book title, song title, story, or twist repeats a week of unit 1 or unit 2 (the U1 fix moved the week 9 twist away from week 2; the page 7 Pip hint is the unit 1 device, U5); the read-alongs sit above decoding level and the decodables sit at it; the letters and sounds are described correctly in every A1/A2/A6 note that I read (for example 's says zzz in has', 'the letters o and u say oo in you', 'the letter o says oh, its letter name, in no').

Cross-checks: the D3 question page numbers use the small-book mapping (cover 1, title 2, story pages 3 to 10) and every answer that I checked points at the right page (for example week 11 'Where is Pat? — sofa (page 7)' = story page 5; week 10 'Where are the shoes? — shoes (page 8)' = story page 6). The book map sticker numbers run 1 to 7 across weeks 9 to 15 and the unit sticker goes after number 7. The song leaders cycle tables 4, 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2 across weeks 9 to 15, as the fix 84b9e68 claims. The word walls grow week by week with no lost word.
